objective: Give every service in the rootfs topology a systemd unit that matches its declared ordering and restart policy, and make the BSP validator fail when a declared service has no unit or a unit contradicts the YAML.
decision_supported: Does the rootfs topology describe services that exist, and can a service be added without its unit going unnoticed?
acceptance: Each of the five services that had no unit now has a unit template with the After, Requires, Restart and StartLimitBurst values its YAML row states.

bsp/validation/validate_manifests.py fails when a YAML service has no unit, when a unit has no YAML row, when the restart policy disagrees, or when the unit orders after something the YAML does not declare.
Every unit keeps NoNewPrivileges=true, ProtectSystem=strict and ProtectHome=true, matching the camera unit that already had them.
No unit in the topology is ordered before robot-safety-monitor except the three that cannot enable an actuator, and each exemption is asserted rather than assumed.
actuator_enable_during_boot stays false by construction: the ordering test is transitive, so a new unit cannot be inserted ahead of the monitor by accident.
All units pass systemd-analyze verify where the tool is available, and the test skips with a reason where it is not.
The restart: no value in the YAML is quoted, because YAML 1.1 reads a bare no as False and the validator was silently comparing a boolean to a string.
evidence: validate_manifests.py: PASS, with the new topology check running.
systemd-analyze verify runs inside tests/hardware/test_service_topology.py for every unit, and the test skips with a reason where the tool is absent.
pytest tests/hardware/test_service_topology.py: 38 passed, including a real systemd-analyze verify run for every unit.
The failure paths: changing a unit Restart to always fails the validator with the service named; deleting a unit fails it with the service named.
The YAML boolean trap: before quoting, robot-update-agent restart parsed as False and the validator reported it, which is how the defect was found.
ruff check and ruff format --check clean; make docs PASS.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: A boot would have to be performed to claim the ordering works on a device; no device is available and the evidence is container and static.
A systemd-analyze result would have to be quoted as a boot result; it is a parse check, not a start check, and the pull request labels it that way.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to bsp/rootfs/libexec/** or to the board manifest.
data_classification: Repository-local YAML, systemd unit templates and Python. No credentials, private data or unreviewed assets.
model_policy: Deterministic Python, pytest and systemd-analyze; no model inference and no network access added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: The units name /usr/libexec/workbench/* binaries that this repository does not ship, so systemd-analyze reports them missing. That is expected for a template and is filtered by name rather than by ignoring the whole output.

Three units are exempt from ordering after the safety monitor. The exemption is a named set with an asserted reason, so a fourth cannot be added quietly, and each exempt unit is asserted to be safety_authority: false.
The ExecStart binaries do not exist, so nothing here proves a service starts. It proves the unit parses and the topology is internally consistent, which is what the issue asks for and no more.
Rollback is a revert of this commit: the five units disappear and the validator stops checking them. Nothing runs these units yet.
